thought: the weight of iron against the log on our agility course
line: You'd go through the log on our course in that iron, not over it.

thought: so much metal it looks like they brought the smithy along
line: Is it iron you're wearing, or are you carrying the anvil as well?

thought: dark grey all over, like soot
line: Grey from top to toe. Did a chimney fall on you, human?

thought: nets on the course are made for gnomes, not iron
line: Kar, the nets on our course were never meant to hold that much iron.

thought: iron is one step above bronze, and they've stopped there
line: One step up from bronze, and you've sat down for a rest on it?

thought: anyone can wear iron without training, which is the trouble
line: Anyone can wear iron, human, which is rather the trouble with it.

thought: points the clanking stranger out to a neighbour, then remembers manners
line: Here, listen to that one clank. No, don't point.

thought: gnomeball is all tackling, but tackling iron would hurt the gnome
line: We'd not tackle you at gnomeball in that, human. We'd bounce.

thought: another heavy one, and the speaker's on glider duty today
line: Iron again, and I'm on the glider today. Kar.

thought: heard a middling smith can hammer it out of a few bars; not special
line: They say any middling smith can knock that up from a few bars.

thought: heard them coming from inside the Tree before seeing them
line: I heard you from up the Tree, human, and I was having a nap.

thought: the trainers tell slow runners their granny is quicker
line: The trainers would say your granny's quicker, in all that iron.

thought: our battle tortoises carry three riders and still outpace this
line: Our battle tortoises go faster than that, human, with three aboard.

thought: Rometti, who dresses so well, would be overcome by plain iron
line: Rometti would take one look at that iron and need a lie down.

thought: all that iron looks hot; a gnome thinks of a drink
line: Warm day for all that iron, human. There's punch at Blurberry's.

thought: polished steel, the speaker sees a reflection
line: Polished steel! I can see the whole Tree in it, human.

thought: bright steel would be easy to spot from a glider
line: Good bright steel. You'd be easy to find from a glider, human.

thought: the steel has been well kept, not a mark on it
line: Somebody kept that steel well. Not a spot on it.

thought: steel is ore and coal cooked together; a gnome thinks of recipes
line: Iron and coal, cooked properly. We'd call that a good recipe.

thought: heard steel needs coal as well as ore, so someone worked for it
line: They say steel takes coal as well as ore. Somebody worked for that.

thought: the shine would make a landing light for the glider at the top
line: That one would make a fine landing light for Captain Errdo.

thought: well fitted, the way Rometti would cut it
line: Very smart, human. Rometti couldn't have cut it better.

thought: the gnome children will want to see themselves in it
line: Megal, steel! The children will be checking their faces in you.

thought: steel this clean, and the speaker's own pots never look like that
line: Steel, and properly kept... my own pots never look like that.

thought: a well turned-out visitor deserves the king's own courtesy
line: Good of you to stop by in your best steel, human.

thought: steel is the sensible step up from iron, and sense is rare in big folk
line: Steel's a sensible step up from iron, and sense is rare in big folk.

thought: they wear it as if they mean to keep it nice
line: You wear that steel like you mean to keep it nice, human.

thought: shiny like the glasses at the cocktail bar
line: Shiny as the glasses at Blurberry's, that steel.

thought: most humans clank; this one rings like a bell
line: Most big folk clank, human, but you rather chime.

thought: polished armour and good manners at the gate
line: Bright steel and good manners. Welcome to the Stronghold, human.

thought: rare red armour and it's spotless
line: Ooh, dragon armour, and you've kept it so clean, human!

thought: heard the red metal comes off fierce beasts, not a forge
line: They say that red metal comes off fierce beasts, not out of a forge.

thought: nobody wears it without a great deal of training
line: You've the training for that red armour, human, and it shows.

thought: points the red out to a neighbour; it means danger was met
line: Look at the red on that one. Somebody's been somewhere dangerous.

thought: all that red, and the speaker in the same green as ever
line: Red armour... and me in the same green for years.

thought: that red would look fine painted on a glider
line: That red would look very well on a glider wing, human.

thought: after earning that, a drink; and there's a cocktail with dragon in it
line: You'll be wanting a cocktail after earning that, human. Drunk dragon?

thought: red suits a big frame; on a gnome it would look like a tomato
line: Red suits a big frame, human. On a gnome it'd look like a tomato.

thought: never seen dragon metal this close
line: Great Guthix, that's dragon metal, isn't it? Up close and all!

thought: rarer than a quiet game of gnomeball
line: Rare as a quiet gnomeball match, that red.

thought: Rometti would want to know where the colour came from
line: Lovely colour. Rometti would ask where you had it dyed.

thought: the red next to the Tree makes the leaves look greener
line: Stand by the Tree in that, human, and the leaves look greener.

thought: dear stuff, worn as if it were everyday
line: Dear stuff, that red metal, and you wear it like a work shirt.

thought: caught out by grand armour in an old hat
line: Is that dragon? And me without my good hat on!

thought: the gnome children will follow the red about
line: The children will follow you round all day in that red, human.

thought: armour fit for dragons, worn to stroll under a tree
line: Dragon armour to walk under a tree, human? Are the leaves that fierce?

thought: paid a high price to look like a piece of fruit
line: Paid a fortune to look like a ripe apple, didn't you, human?

thought: heard it drops off metal dragons; this lot looks bought
line: Metal dragons drop that, they say. Yours looks bought, human.

thought: all that grand metal and still blowing at the foot of the ramp
line: All that dragon metal, and out of breath at the foot of the ramp.

thought: the speaker just painted their own door red, and now it looks dull
line: Red armour, and I've just painted my door red. Now it looks dull.

thought: every big one in red wants a glider, and the glider pays
line: Every big one in red wants a glider ride. Poor glider.

thought: years of training to end up looking like a redberry
line: That's a great deal of training to look like a redberry, human.

thought: gnomeball is all tackling; that armour wouldn't last the game
line: Wear that to gnomeball and we'd have it off you by the second goal.

thought: all the money went on the armour, none on the face
line: Look, red armour and a plain face. Spent it all on the armour, then.

thought: too bright to hide in the woods round here
line: Very bright, human. I'd not try hiding in our woods in that.

thought: it came off a dragon; did it not want it back?
line: So red, human! Did the dragon not want it back?

thought: the price of it, measured in gliders
line: Must've cost a glider or two, that red. Was it worth it, human?

thought: so much red it looks like a warning sign
line: Great Guthix, red! Are you meant to be a warning, human?

thought: bright red in a town where every gnome carries a bow
line: In a town where even the cooks carry bows, you wear red, human?

thought: the bar's a floor up, for when the red gets heavy
line: The bar's a floor up, human, if the red's getting heavy.

thought: a whip is quick, and gnomes value quick
line: Quick weapon, that whip. Gnomes do like a quick thing.

thought: heard whips drop off abyssal demons; that's earned
line: Off an abyssal demon, they say. You'll have earned that, human.

thought: spots the barb at the end, worries for the leaves
line: Ooh, is that a barb on the end of your whip? Mind the leaves.

thought: tells the neighbours to give the whip some room, respectfully
line: That one's got a whip from the Abyss. Stand back a bit, all of us.

thought: only a well-trained hand can hold one
line: Only a well-trained hand holds one of those, human, and steady too.

thought: segmented red and black, like the king worms from the swamp
line: Red and black and all in segments... like a king worm, only fiercer.

thought: heard it's strong and not too dear; a sensible pick
line: Sensible choice, a whip. Strong and not too dear, they say.

thought: the long lash sways like a branch
line: Great Guthix, it moves like a branch in the wind!

thought: with that, nobody at gnomeball would dare tackle them
line: Swing that at gnomeball and nobody would tackle you, human.

thought: lots of fighters carry one, this one is kept well
line: Lots of fighters come through with a whip, human. Yours is kept nice.

thought: the children would love to hear it crack once
line: Does it crack? Go on, human, crack it once for the children.

thought: handy for catching toads in the swamp
line: I'd borrow that whip for catching toads, if you'd let me, human.

thought: a barbed whip, coiled neatly; a sign of good upbringing
line: A barbed whip, and coiled neat. Somebody was raised properly.

thought: steady hands like that would do for a glider
line: Steady hands like that, human, and Captain Errdo would let you fly.

thought: a whip from the Abyss is rare up in the trees
line: Megal, a whip from the Abyss, isn't it? You don't see many up here.

thought: half the fighters up the ramp carry the same whip
line: A whip, human? Half the fighters who come up the ramp carry one.

thought: a whip looks like something for driving the battle tortoises
line: Do you drive tortoises with that, human? Nacklepen might hire you.

thought: yet another whip, there must be a shop for them
line: Another whip. Is there a shop for them somewhere?

thought: heard it comes off a demon; hopes the demon was finished off
line: Off a demon, they say. Did you check it's quite dead, human?

thought: a long lash in a clumsy hand will take an ear
line: You'd have your own ear off with that, human.

thought: so many whips, and nobody offers to beat a rug
line: Whip, whip, whip... and not one of them ever offers to beat a rug.

thought: big folk crack their whips under the Tree and frighten the leaves
line: Every big one with a whip cracks it under the Tree. The leaves!

thought: the barb near the bark; the Tree was here first
line: Keep that barb off the bark, human, the Tree was here first.

thought: no cracking near the bar, the glasses
line: Kar, no cracking it near the bar, human. Blurberry's glasses.

thought: gnomes would rather use a bow and stand further off
line: Showy things, whips. We use a bow and stand further back.

thought: took it for a rope at first; same thing to a gnome
line: A rope, is it? Oh, a whip... same thing, to a gnome.

thought: gnomeball has few rules, but surely one is no whips
line: Gnomeball has very few rules, human, but no whips is one of them.

thought: red and black like a burnt batta
line: Red and black, like a burnt batta. Somebody should have watched it.

thought: points out that someone's brought a whip to visit a tree
line: Look, that one's brought a whip to see a tree. A tree!

thought: Gulluck sells proper weapons up the Tree
line: Gulluck sells proper weapons up the Tree, human, if you tire of that.

thought: the teal of the blade is like the river on a clear morning
line: That teal's the colour of the river on a clear morning, human.

thought: heard only a near-master smith can forge one
line: Only a near-master smith can forge one of those, they say.

thought: second-best scimitar, and second is a fine place to be
line: Second-best scimitar going, and second is a fine place to be.

thought: a blade like that, and the speaker thinks of peeling oranges
line: Rune... I could peel a lot of oranges with that.

thought: Gulluck the weapon seller would want a look at it
line: Gulluck would like a look at that, human. He's a floor above the bar.

thought: a rune blade near the Tree, mind the bark
line: Megal, a rune blade! Mind it near the bark, human.

thought: tells a neighbour to look at the colour of the blade
line: That one's got a rune scimitar. Look at the colour of it.

thought: fire giants drop them, so maybe they fought one
line: Did you take that off a fire giant, human? Brave, if so.

thought: they keep their edge better than the gnome cooks do
line: You keep that edge well, human. Our cooks could learn from you.

thought: curved and quick, close to a gnome's taste
line: Curved and quick, that blade. Very nearly gnomish, human.

thought: can't decide on the colour, settles on teal
line: Is that blue, or green? Teal, I'd say.

thought: a long fall off the ramp, so carry the point down
line: Hold it point down on the ramp, human, it's a long way to fall.

thought: fire giants carry those and the speaker has a butter knife
line: Fire giants drop those, and here's me with a butter knife.

thought: they'd make a good guard for the Tree
line: You'd make a fine guard for the Tree with that, human.

thought: a wicked blade and a kind face, odd pair
line: Wicked blade, kind face. Funny pair, but it works.

thought: the jagged edge looks like a bread knife
line: A dragon scimitar! Jagged on the edge like a bread knife.

thought: heard it's the best scimitar there is
line: Best scimitar there is, they say, and it shows, human.

thought: under the Tree, blades stay sheathed; the floor's just swept
line: Keep it sheathed under the Tree, human. We've just swept.

thought: can't be smithed, so somebody found it
line: Nobody smiths those from raw metal. Somebody found it, then.

thought: jagged like a saw, a gnome thinks of planks
line: Ooh, jagged like a saw! Could you cut me a plank with it?

thought: points out the toothed blade, warns others back
line: Look at that one's blade, all teeth. Don't stand too close.

thought: heard there's none better; a gnome would still take a bow
line: They say there's no better scimitar. I'd still take a bow.

thought: blood-red and jagged, not table cutlery
line: Blood-red and jagged. Not something you'd bring to the dinner table.

thought: fighting folk get hungry; crunchies at the bar
line: There's toad crunchies at the bar, human, if you've been fighting.

thought: can't be smithed; then who sharpens it?
line: Can't smith them, they say. Then who sharpens them, I wonder?

thought: the red blade flashing in the light
line: Great Guthix, is that dragon? Mind it doesn't catch the sun, human.

thought: most fighters carry a whip; a scimitar's a change
line: Most who come through carry a whip. A scimitar's a nice change, human.

thought: curved like a glider's wing, only nastier
line: Curved like a glider's wing, that blade, but nastier.

thought: everyone wants the best blade, nobody sweeps up after
line: Everyone wants the best blade. Nobody wants to sweep up after.

thought: far too much blade for the swamp toads
line: That'd make short work of the swamp toads, human. Too short.

thought: green is the gnomes' colour, and they wear it smaller
line: Green, human? That's our colour, and we wear it smaller.

thought: scaly green leather, like a swamp toad that gave up
line: Scaly green leather. Looks like a toad gave up halfway.

thought: heard it's real dragonhide; the dragon wore it better
line: Real dragonhide, they say. The dragon wore it better, I expect.

thought: a big one in green, looking like a hedge
line: Here, look, the big one's dressed as a hedge.

thought: dragon hunters come in from the Wilderness wanting drinks
line: They come up from the Wilderness in green and want a cocktail first.

thought: Rometti will have opinions on that shade of green
line: Green again... Rometti will have something to say about that green.

thought: did the dragon fight, or was it asleep?
line: Did the dragon put up a fight, human, or was it asleep?

thought: archer's leather on someone who walks like a swordsman
line: Archer's leather, and you walk like a swordsman, human.

thought: heard the dragon hunters get set upon themselves
line: Hunted green dragons, did you? They say the hunters get hunted.

thought: scales and all; do they shed?
line: Scales and all. Do you shed, human?

thought: creaky leather wouldn't survive gnomeball
line: Leather that creaks like that wouldn't last one game of gnomeball.

thought: saw green and thought, for a moment, a gnome
line: Green! I took you for one of us, human, till I saw the leather.

thought: archers in leather, and none as good as a gnome child with a bow
line: Archers in leather, and not one of them as good as a gnome child.

thought: the hide is tougher than the one inside it
line: Hide that's tougher than the one wearing it, human?

thought: wears dragon, walks like a tortoise
line: Wears dragon and walks like a tortoise.

thought: heard it's paid for in marks of grace, that's a lot of laps
line: Paid for in marks of grace, they say. That's a lot of laps, human.

thought: the hood hides most of the face; shy or just quick
line: That hood hides most of the face. Shy, or just quick?

thought: the trainers would have nothing to shout about
line: The trainers would have nothing to shout at you about, human.

thought: a runner, barely puffed after the ramp
line: Ooh, a runner! Barely puffed, and up our ramp too.

thought: dressed as if racing the glider
line: Look at that one. Dressed like they mean to race the glider.

thought: the speaker could do with light clothes, always last up the ladder
line: Light clothes... I ought to get some. I'm always last up the ladder.

thought: would be past the wingers and through the net
line: You'd be past the wingers and through the net in that, human.

thought: offers a sit at the bar, though they don't need the rest
line: Get your breath back at Blurberry's, human. Not that you need to.

thought: most big folk clank in plate; this is a nice change
line: Most big folk clank through in plate. This makes a nice change.

thought: a runner's outfit on someone who actually runs
line: A runner's outfit, worn by a runner. Not often we see that, human.

thought: heard the cloth gives a runner breath back quicker
line: They say that cloth gives a runner breath back quicker. It shows.

thought: would race a terrorbird and lose with dignity
line: You'd race a terrorbird in that and lose with dignity, human.

thought: took the hooded figure for a ghost at first
line: A ghost? No, a runner in a hood... good afternoon, then!

thought: paid for in laps rather than coin, an honest outfit
line: Clothes that cost laps, not coin. That's an honest outfit, human.

thought: there's a balloon south of the Tree, but they'd beat it on foot
line: There's a balloon south of the Tree, human, but you'd beat it on foot.

thought: all those laps for a hood that covers the eyes
line: All those laps for a hood, human, and you can't even see out of it.

thought: dressed for rooftops, but our course is so gentle nobody falls
line: Dressed for the rooftops, human? Nobody even falls off our course.

thought: hood up, face hidden; either shy or owes the bar
line: Hood up, face hidden. Either shy or owes Blurberry money.

thought: heard the cloth helps get breath back; do they need it?
line: They say that cloth helps you get your breath back. Need it, do you?

thought: the trainers would still say their granny is quicker
line: The trainers would still say your granny's quicker, human.

thought: clothes for roofs, and gnomes live in trees
line: Clothes for running on roofs, human, and we live in a tree.

thought: another hood, the speaker never knows who anybody is
line: Another one in a hood. I'll never learn who anybody is.

thought: rooftop runners will be up the Tree and on the gliders next
line: Rooftop runners. They'll be up the Tree next, and on the gliders.

thought: light clothes on a heavy step, the clothes are trying
line: Light clothes for a heavy step, human. They're doing their best.

thought: dressed for speed, and the gliders still go faster
line: All dressed up for running, human, and the gliders still go faster.

thought: they call it graceful; the ladder will tell
line: Graceful, is it? We'll see on the ladder.

thought: the hood makes them look like a sack of flour
line: That hood makes you look like a sack of flour on legs, human.

thought: dressed for a race nobody else is running
line: Here, look at this one, dressed for a race nobody's running.

thought: marks of grace are just picking things up off the floor
line: Marks of grace, was it? We'd have called that picking things up.

thought: running clothes where even the cooks are quicker
line: Running clothes, human, where even the cooks are quicker than you?

thought: heard six brothers wore gear like that; wonders which
line: Six brothers wore that sort of gear, they say. Wonder which this was.

thought: the speaker thought their own hat was old
line: Old, old armour... and I thought my good hat was old.

thought: old gear; does it creak, or is it the wearer?
line: Ooh, old armour! Does it creak, human, or is that you?

thought: tells a neighbour it's hand-me-downs
line: Look at the old armour on that one. Hand-me-downs, I'd say.

thought: Rometti would at least want it brushed
line: Funny old gear, human. Rometti would want it brushed, at least.

thought: gear like that has a story, best not asked
line: Gear like that has a story in it, human, and I'd not ask.

thought: where do big folk find such things? not in any shop
line: Where do they find it all, these big folk? Not in any shop I know.

thought: the armour looks as if it remembers every fight
line: Old armour. Looks like it remembers every fight.

thought: plainly not new, answers itself
line: That's not new, is it, human? Not by a long way.

thought: big folk buy new blades and wear old armour, backwards
line: Big folk buy new blades and wear old armour. Backwards, that is.

thought: took it for rust, then saw it's meant to look that way
line: Is that rust? No... that's just how it's meant to look.

thought: old things do well round the old Tree
line: Come and sit by the Tree, human. Old things do well round here.

thought: where did that come from? better not to know
line: Great Guthix, where did that come from? Don't tell me, human.

thought: the stranger is wearing half a museum
line: Here, that one's wearing half a museum.

thought: old gear and a tired face; which looks older?
line: Old gear and a new face. Can't decide which looks more tired.

thought: heard you can't buy one; they went and got it
line: Can't buy one of those, they say. You went and got it, human.

thought: all those flames and no light at all, odd and lovely
line: All those flames and it gives off no light at all. Odd, and lovely.

thought: thought the Tree had caught fire; it's only the cape
line: Megal! I thought the Tree had caught, and it's only you, human.

thought: every wave; a gnome would have taken the glider home
line: Every wave of the Fight Cave, human? We'd have taken the glider home.

thought: beat TzTok-Jad; that earns a cocktail
line: TzTok-Jad, was it? You'll not want for a cocktail here, human.

thought: the children will want to warm their hands at it
line: Look, the fire one. The children will want to warm their hands.

thought: a fire cape on the ramp, and the speaker's batta has gone cold
line: A fire cape on the ramp, and here's me with a damp batta.

thought: the shifting orange looks like a sunset that won't settle
line: Like a sunset that won't sit still, that cape.

thought: not many come up the ramp in one of those
line: Not many come up our ramp wearing one of those, human.

thought: offers a seat by the fire, then sees they've brought their own
line: There's a seat by the fire for you, human... well, you've your own.

thought: heard it's every wave and then the big fiery one
line: Through every wave, they say, and the big fiery one at the end.

thought: the pattern flows; does it always do that?
line: Ooh! Does it flicker like that all the time, human?

thought: the cape suits the leaves, like autumn
line: That cape suits the leaves, human. Autumn all year round.

thought: others boast of the cave; this one just wears the cape
line: Half the big folk boast about the Fight Cave. You just wear the cape.

thought: couldn't sell it if they wanted, and why would they
line: Couldn't sell it if they wanted to, and why would they?

thought: all those flames and no light; can't even read by them
line: A fire cape and no light off it? Can't even read by you, human.

thought: does it toast crunchies? if not, what's it for
line: Does it toast crunchies, human? Then what's it for?

thought: can't be bought, so no shop to blame for the look
line: Can't be bought, they say, so there's no shop to blame, human.

thought: someone fetch a bucket for the burning cape
line: Look, the one with the burning cape. Somebody fetch a bucket.

thought: did the beast at the end have nothing in green?
line: Did TzTok-Jad not have anything in green, human?

thought: lava capes on the ramp now, next they'll bring the lava
line: Lava capes on the ramp now... next they'll bring the lava along.

thought: looks fit to set a glider alight, so walk
line: That cape looks fit to set a glider alight. You'll walk, human.

thought: so many fire capes lately; is the cave giving them away?
line: Fire capes everywhere lately. Is the cave giving them away?

thought: looks hot but gives no light; just showing off
line: Looks hot, but it's only showing off.

thought: stood in a cave for it; a gnome would have sent a tortoise
line: Stood in a cave for that, human? We'd have sent a tortoise.

thought: the gnome children made one of autumn leaves, quieter
line: Our children made one out of autumn leaves. Theirs was quieter.

thought: the cape flickers; is it the cape or their nerve?
line: Is it the cape that flickers, human, or your nerve?

thought: every fire cape tells the same story at the bar
line: Every one in a fire cape tells the same story at the bar.

thought: a cape of fire, and the swamp toads still aren't frightened
line: You've a cape of fire, human, and the toads still aren't scared.

thought: the pattern can't settle, much like its owner
line: Shifts about like it can't settle, human. Like its owner.

thought: black rock and lava worn like a shawl
line: Black rock and lava, worn like a shawl. Big folk are odd.

thought: the cape moves as if alive
line: Great Guthix, it's moving! Is it meant to move, human?

thought: heard you beat TzKal-Zuk for one; the speaker would have stayed home
line: Beat TzKal-Zuk for one of those, they say. I'd have stayed home.

thought: cracked with a glow between, like the oven door
line: Cracks all over, and the glow in between... like my oven door.

thought: someone wearing a lava flow; don't stand downhill
line: Here, look, the one wearing a lava flow. Don't stand downhill.

thought: offers a cool drink if the cape is warm
line: There's a cool drink at Blurberry's, human, if that's warm.

thought: lava is an odd thing to want on the back
line: An odd thing to want on your back, lava. Takes all sorts, human.

thought: a lava cape in a tree town; will check the leaves after
line: A lava cape in a tree town... I'll be checking the leaves after.

thought: is that rock? it is, glowing rock
line: Is that rock? It's rock that glows.

thought: big folk and their heavy capes; a gnome would make it lighter
line: Big folk and their capes. A gnome would've made it lighter.

thought: heard it's from the bottom of the Inferno; who goes to the bottom
line: The bottom of the Inferno, they say. Who'd go to the bottom of that?

thought: wearing what they warn the children about
line: That one's wearing the stuff they warn the children about.

thought: toad crunchies would cook on that
line: Toad crunchies would cook on that, human, I'd wager.

thought: cool on top and hot underneath, like a chocolate bomb
line: Cooled on top and hot underneath, like a good chocolate bomb.

thought: not many come by with one, fewer stop to chat
line: Not many come by with one of those, human. Fewer stop to chat.

thought: a pointed hat, many points; gnome taste
line: Points on your hat, and more than one! You've gnome taste, human.

thought: heard they come out of crackers; someone pulled the other end
line: Out of a cracker, they say, and somebody had to pull the other end.

thought: whoever pulled that cracker picked the colour well
line: Whoever pulled that cracker chose well.

thought: took it for a crown, then saw a partyhat, nearly as good
line: A crown? Oh, a partyhat... nearly as good, human.

thought: wearing Christmas on its head all year
line: That one's wearing Christmas on its head, all year.

thought: bright like the fruit at Heckel's stall
line: Bright as the fruit at Heckel's stall, that hat.

thought: the speaker pulled a cracker once and the other one picked
line: I pulled a cracker once. The other one got to pick.

thought: the hat would do nicely up the Tree at Christmas
line: That hat would do nicely up the Tree at Christmas, human.

thought: festive without a sprig of holly
line: Very festive, human, and not a sprig of holly in sight.

thought: every point straight; somebody keeps it in a box
line: All those points and not one bent. Somebody keeps that hat in a box.

thought: the children would love a look at the hat
line: Ooh, a partyhat! May the children have a look, human?

thought: the hat cheers up even a big face
line: Even a big face looks cheerful under that hat, human.

thought: Rometti couldn't have picked a better colour
line: Rometti couldn't have picked a better colour for you, human.

thought: the hat is a long way up; a gnome admires it from below
line: That hat's a long way up, human. We gnomes admire it from here.

thought: pull a cracker with a gnome and you get to pick
line: Pull a cracker with a gnome some time, human. We let you pick.

thought: someone pulled the other end; where are they now?
line: Somebody pulled the other end of that cracker. Where are they, human?

thought: all those points, none of them a good idea
line: All those points on your hat, human, and none of them a good idea.

thought: Christmas up on their tall head, not down here
line: Is it Christmas up there, human? It's not down here.

thought: somebody should tell them the party's over
line: Somebody tell that one the party's over.

thought: no brim, rain in the eyes
line: A hat with no brim, human? You'll get rain in your eyes.

thought: shaped like a crown, and nobody bows
line: Crown-shaped, human, and still nobody's bowing.

thought: every big one in a partyhat thinks the Tree should stop and look
line: Every big one in a partyhat thinks the Tree should stop and look.

thought: so many points; one is plenty for a gnome
line: Points everywhere on that hat. One's plenty, if you ask a gnome.

thought: did they pick the colour, or lose the pull?
line: Did you pick the colour, human, or were you the one who lost the pull?

thought: a lot of hat for a walk under a tree
line: Bit much for a walk under a tree, isn't it, human?

thought: whose party is it? not theirs, by the look
line: Whose party is it, human? Not yours, by the look of it.

thought: that hat would come off at the first net on the course
line: You'd lose that on the agility course, human, at the first net.

thought: heard they only turn up at Christmas; must be a long Christmas
line: They say those only turn up at Christmas. Must be a long Christmas.

thought: one cracker, one hat, a great deal of fuss
line: One cracker, one hat, and a great deal of fuss.

thought: dressed for a party and come to a tree
line: Dressed for a party, human, and you've come to see a tree.

thought: heard nobody else can even put one on
line: They say nobody else can even put one of those on.

thought: gems on a cape; Rometti would need to sit
line: Gems on the back of a cape! Rometti would need a sit down.

thought: every craft, so they'd know how to fold a glider wing
line: Every craft, human? Then you'll know how to fold a glider wing.

thought: the speaker's battas never rise, and there goes one who's done everything
line: My battas never rise, and that one's done every craft there is.

thought: a long cape, it'd trail twice over on a gnome
line: Very long cape. It'd trail on the floor on a gnome... twice.

thought: done everything; gnome cooking too?
line: Gnome cooking too, I wonder? That one's done everything else.

thought: the collar is smart, the rest is a lot of cape
line: That collar's very smart, human. The rest is a lot of cape.

thought: they'll know the course; the trainers can't shout at them
line: You'll know our agility course, then, human. The trainers can't shout.

thought: gnomes have no cape for every craft, they just get on with it
line: We've no cape for every craft. A gnome just gets on with it.

thought: the gems; doesn't it pull at the neck?
line: Ooh, the cape with the gems! Doesn't it pull at the neck, human?

thought: every craft must be tiring; rest a while
line: Rest your feet a while, human. Every craft must be tiring.

thought: a fruit blast at the bar, fit for that cape
line: Blurberry's mixing a fruit blast, human. Fit for a cape like that.

thought: gold edging and red gems, very sure of themselves
line: Gold edging and red gems. Somebody's very sure of themselves.

thought: is that the cape for... yes, it is
line: Is that the cape for... yes, it is. Well I never.

thought: did it take a long while? of course it did
line: Did it take a long while, human? Silly question, of course it did.

thought: every gnome carries a bow, none has that one
line: Every gnome carries a bow, human, and not one of us has that one.

thought: hooked tips and a yellow-green string; the string especially
line: Hooked tips and a yellow-green string. Very nice, the string.

thought: heard it comes from the Chambers of Xeric, a long way off
line: From the Chambers of Xeric, they say. A long walk for a bow, human.

thought: the speaker has had the same bow since they were small
line: Same bow since I was a sapling, me. And now look.

thought: a twisted bow; the children will want to see, from a distance
line: A twisted bow! The children will want a look, human, from back here.

thought: heard they're rare and dearer than a glider
line: Rare as anything, those, and dearer than a glider, they say.

thought: they hold it like it might break; quite right
line: You hold it like it might break, human. Quite right.

thought: the tortoise archers would give their hats for it
line: The archers on the tortoises would give their hats for that bow.

thought: black limbs, white streaks, like a magpie made into a bow
line: Black limbs, white streaks. Like a magpie made into a bow.

thought: a gnome would need a ladder to draw it
line: We'd need a ladder to draw that, human. You make it look easy.

thought: hooked tips; mind the low branches
line: Mind the low branches with those hooked tips, human.

thought: from under a mountain in Kebos, and the speaker never left the Tree
line: From under a mountain in Kebos... and I've never left the Tree.

thought: makes the gnomes' bows look like toothpicks
line: That bow makes ours look like toothpicks, human.

thought: a twisted bow; better not hold it, might faint
line: Great Guthix, a twisted bow! Don't let me hold it, human, I'd faint.

thought: carrying the dearest thing in the Stronghold, and smiling
line: That one's carrying the dearest thing in the Stronghold, and smiling.

thought: heard it's never sold for coins; can see why
line: Never sold for coins, they say. I can see why, human.

thought: a knight with no horse, not even a tortoise
line: A knight with no horse, human? Not even a tortoise?

thought: one of those knights; act natural
line: Here, look, it's one of those knights. Act natural.

thought: the pieces look like two outfits that had an argument
line: Looks like two outfits that had an argument.

thought: Rometti could fit them for something nicer, it'd take a while
line: Rometti could fit you for something nicer, human. It'd take a while.

thought: all that work for the knights, paid in a nightshirt
line: All that work for the knights, and they paid you in a nightshirt?

thought: so sombre; is there a funeral on?
line: Very sombre, human. Is somebody's funeral on?

thought: did the knights let them pick the colour?
line: Did the knights let you pick the colour, human? I'd ask again.

thought: thought it was a knight, it's only the outfit
line: Ooh, a knight! Oh, it's just someone dressed as one.

thought: the knights can keep it; gnomes look better in green
line: Kar, the knights can keep their gear. Gnomes look better in green.

thought: the knights' gear; prize or punishment?
line: That one's in the knights' gear. Was it a prize or a punishment?

thought: if it's a uniform, the knights need a new tailor
line: Is it a uniform, human? Then the knights want a new tailor.

thought: the children will think it's a crow
line: You'll frighten the children, human. They'll take you for a crow.

thought: knights are allowed to smile
line: Cheer up a bit, human. Knights are allowed to smile, I think.

thought: all knight and no shine
line: All knight and no shine. Somebody forgot the polish.

thought: a cape that was given, not bought, the best sort
line: A cape given, not bought. That's the best sort, human.

thought: heard it's Saradomin's own gift; they must have shown him something
line: A gift from Saradomin himself, they say. You showed him something.

thought: a battle mage; gnomes don't go in for magic much
line: A battle mage, then. Gnomes don't go in for magic much.

thought: Brimstail by the river talks magic
line: Brimstail's cave is by the river, human, if you want to talk magic.

thought: Saradomin's blue, mind it near the swamp
line: Ooh, Saradomin's blue! Mind it near the swamp, human.

thought: a battle mage, Saradomin's own gift
line: That one's a battle mage, look. Saradomin's own gift, that cape.

thought: the blue is the sky over the Grand Tree on a good day
line: That blue's the sky over Ta Quir Priw on a good day, human.

thought: a cape from a god; the speaker's came off a stall
line: From a god, that cape. Mine came off a market stall.

thought: Saradomin chose well, and a Guthix gnome says so
line: Saradomin chose well, human. That's a gnome of Guthix saying it.

thought: mages are rare here; stay for a drink and tell it
line: Mages are rare up here, human. Stay for a cocktail and tell us all.

thought: deep blue, calming among the green
line: Deep blue, human. Very calming, among all this green.

thought: proven to a god; a gnome would settle for a goal
line: Proven yourself to a god, human. We'd settle for a gnomeball goal.

thought: Saradomin's cape on a quiet street
line: Is that Saradomin's cape? On a quiet street like ours!

thought: Rometti sells blue, but not a blue like that
line: Rometti sells blue, human, but not a blue like that.

thought: the children pray to Guthix, but they'll stare at that cape
line: Our children say prayers to Guthix, human, but they'll stare at that.

thought: gnomes like a thing done properly, and the cape says done
line: We gnomes like a thing done properly, and that cape says done.

thought: heard they're bought from the master, and dear
line: Bought from the master, they say, and dear. Worth it, human.

thought: the emblem on the back; someone's very good at something
line: That emblem on the back... somebody's very good at something.

thought: a master's cape; which one? let me guess
line: Which master's cape is that, human? No, let me guess.

thought: if it's the cooking one, the bar is always hiring
line: If that's the cooking one, human, Blurberry's always hiring.

thought: a cape that stops you burning things; would never take it off
line: If I'd a cape that stopped me burning things, I'd never take it off.

thought: a master, walking about like anyone
line: Look at that one's cape. A master, and walking about like anyone.

thought: one thing done perfectly, a very gnomish way to live
line: One thing done perfectly, human. That's a very gnomish way to live.

thought: they'd make a fine teacher for the gnome children
line: You'd make a fine teacher for the gnome children, human.

thought: a master, and the speaker stood in an apron
line: Great Guthix, a master! And here's me stood in my apron.

thought: the best at something, and still stops to look at the Tree
line: The best at something, and you still stop to look at our Tree.

thought: a trim next; one craft is never enough for a gnome
line: A trim on that next, human? One craft's never enough for a gnome.

thought: even Rometti would nod at that cape
line: Even Rometti would nod at that cape, human.

thought: half the big folk can't boil an egg, and here's a master
line: Half the big folk can't boil an egg, and here's a master.

thought: heard only the very best may wear one
line: They say only the very best at a thing may wear one of those.

thought: best at one thing; what about the rest?
line: The best at one thing, human. What about all the others?

thought: paid a master for it; a gnome would have knitted one
line: You paid a master for that, human? We'd have knitted you one.

thought: a master of something, not of walking quietly
line: Here, that one's a master of something. Not of walking quietly.

thought: one craft, done to death, and a cape to prove it
line: One craft, done to death, and a cape to prove it.

thought: a cape for one thing; gnomes do six before breakfast
line: A cape for one thing... gnomes do six things before breakfast.

thought: no trim, so just the one craft
line: No trim on it, human? Just the one craft, then.

thought: not Rometti's cut, plain from here
line: That's not Rometti's cut, human. I can tell from here.

thought: is the cape for something useful, like cooking?
line: Is your cape for something useful, human? Cooking, say?

thought: the hefty sum would feed them at the bar for a season
line: For that sum, human, you'd have eaten at Blurberry's for a season.

thought: a master's cape! oh, that one
line: Ooh, a master's cape! Oh... that one.

thought: every master up the ramp wants the cape admired
line: Every master that comes up the ramp wants the cape admired.

thought: the best at it, and gnomeball would still eat them
line: So you're the best at it. Gnomeball would still eat you, human.

thought: lovely cape, a bit warm for the agility course
line: Lovely cape, human. Bit warm for the agility course, mind.

thought: mastered one thing and stopped, while the Tree kept growing
line: Mastered one thing and stopped, human? The Tree kept growing.

thought: heard only the best may wear one; standards must have slipped
line: Only the best may wear one, they say. Standards must have slipped.
